questions.q: What reacts first to GNSS interference in the EKF?
options: The satellite count in the GPS message
questions.explain: Disagreement between GNSS and the inertial sensors shows up earliest; inertial sensors aren't affected by external interference.

questions.q: Satellites are normal, accuracy is “excellent,” but EKF innovations are growing. This looks like:
options: Sky obstruction by buildings and trees
questions.explain: The measurement contradicts the model despite a “good” fix.

options: Only a message to the operator on the GCS

questions.q: What must the pilot always have when GPS degrades?
options: Non-GPS modes and the skill to fly them
RTL on a switch and a geofence
questions.explain: Geofence and RTL are useless without position.

questions.q: How do you simulate GPS loss in SITL?
questions.explain: In older versions — SIM_GPS_DISABLE = 1. Other scenarios: SIM_GPS1_NOISE, SIM_GPS1_GLTCH_*, SIM_MAG1_OFS_*.

questions.q: What is the right transmitter power at the site?
questions.explain: Excess power jams your neighbors and heats the VTX.

questions.q: What does INAV do on a multicopter if GPS is lost during RTH?
options: Emergency Landing: position is lost, so RTH is impossible
Continues RTH on the last heading
questions.explain: If there is no position for longer than ~2 s, INAV in RTH/WP switches to Emergency Landing: the copter descends in ANGLE at failsafe_throttle and cuts the motors after failsafe_off_delay (with zero values it's effectively a DROP). failsafe_procedure is the reaction to RC loss, not GPS loss; a wing with inav_allow_gps_fix_estimation can continue returning on the estimate.
